title: Gateway-based shadowing with stratified sampling and budgeted throttles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a gateway-level shadowing subsystem that duplicates live requests to candidate models in a way that ensures: safe isolation of mirrored workloads from production state, stratified sampling by customer tier and route, per-customer cost budgets for mirrored traffic, deterministic replay for debug, and clear observability so rollouts and A/B tests can use shadow traffic without risk to latency or cost. This is an incremental design and will be rolled out behind feature flags. The subsystem must support both hosted and dedicated runtimes and integrate with existing rollout policies and auto-rollback signals.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can duplicate requests to up to two shadow targets without increasing 99th pct production latency by >5ms on P50 baseline
Mirrored requests are tagged and routed such that candidate model executions are isolated from production caches (separate KV namespaces) and do not mutate canonical data stores
Sampling rules support stratification by route, customer_tier (free/paid/enterprise), and explicit experiment IDs
Cost throttle enforces configurable token budgets per-customer and global mirror spend budgets; when budget hit, mirror sampling gracefully degrades and logs budget events
All mirrored payloads are stored encrypted and accessible via a replay API that accepts experiment_id + time range and returns anonymized records
Dashboards surface mirror vs production divergence metrics (latency, error-rate, token-cost, token-length distribution) and trigger auto-rollback alerts when defined thresholds are crossed
E2E tests simulate 10k RPS with realistic token distributions to validate isolation and budget behavior in CI job (smoke and stress)
implementation_steps: Design gateway mirror adapter: extend ingress to optionally fork request to mirror chain (feature-flagged)
Implement mirror tag propagation (experiment-id, sample-reason, customer-tier) in headers and traces
Create separate mirror execution namespace for KV/cache and ephemeral model state; ensure no writes reach production DBs
Build stratified sampling engine (rules + weights) with a lightweight evaluator in gateway for sub-ms decision
Add per-customer and global mirror spend tracker integrated with cost-telemetry; implement throttle policy to reduce sample rate when budgets near limit
Persist mirrored records to encrypted S3 with retention policy and anonymization pipeline (PII redaction step)
Expose replay API and a small CLI to request batches for offline eval and log-replay debugging
Add observability: metrics, traces, and pre-built Grafana panels for divergence and mirror spend; wire alerts for thresholds
Create canary rollout playbook: enable mirror for 1% sampled free tier routes -> add enterprise -> increase to target sampling, validate metrics, then flip traffic routing to full canary
End-to-end QA: run CI stress + manual rehearsals; security review and threat model sign-off for mirrored data storage
decisions: Mirror duplication will be done in the gateway layer (not client-side) to centralize sampling and budget enforcement
Mirrored executions use separate KV namespaces to avoid cache poisoning and ensure deterministic replayability
We will enforce a global monthly mirror budget per customer to prevent unexpected billing spikes; budgets configurable per-customer via Console
Anonymization will be mandatory for all stored mirrors; full payloads are encrypted-at-rest and access is logged
Sampling logic will prefer stratified deterministic hashing over pure randomness to ensure reproducible cohorts for A/B comparisons
tradeoffs: Gateway-level duplication centralizes control but increases gateway complexity and coupling to rollout logic
Separate KV namespaces add memory/cost overhead and operational complexity but are required to guarantee isolation
Aggressive anonymization reduces debug fidelity for corner-case failures; we will offer an elevated access path with stricter audit controls for incident investigations
Per-customer budgets may throttle mirror coverage for high-value customers under constrained budgets; we will surface suggested budgets based on sampled estimates
comments: 2025-03-06 - Marco Li: Spike started to measure gateway overhead for duplicating headers+body; initial microbenchmark shows +1.8ms median and +6ms at P99 for small JSON requests. Need to optimize serialization path.
2025-03-07 - Priya Shah (PM): Add requirement to support 'no-mirror' header for partners that cannot allow duplication. Also requested UI knob for per-customer mirror budget.
2025-03-09 - SRE Review: Concern about replay storage RPS; recommend batching writes and using a dedicated ingest cluster to avoid S3 per-request stalls.
2025-03-11 - Security: Approved anonymization approach but asked for formal threat model and retention justification before prod enablement
2025-03-12 - Marco Li: Updated prototype to use zero-copy header references and moved KV isolation into sidecar process; new microbenchmarks drop P99 overhead to +2.5ms
notes: Consider integrating with Redwood Optimize to suggest mirror budgets based on historical token usage per customer
We should align mirror divergence signals with existing auto-rollback system so same thresholds can flip canary traffic back to baseline
Possible future: allow mirrored executions to run against quantized model variants to reduce mirror cost while preserving signal quality
